 ORDER
The present petition has been filed by the petitioners, who are the Deputy Manager and the Chief Manager of the State Bank of India, Main Branch Guna.

sentences.text: At the relevant point of time, they were serving at Morena.
The FIR which is sought to be quashed is Crime No. 561/2022, registered for the offences under Section 420, 409 120-B, 34 of IPC registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Morena.

The brief case against the petitioners is as follows:-
- in September, 2012, the debtor Ashish Shukla was granted a cash credit limit of Rs.
10,00,000/- by the State Bank of India, Morena Branch;
- on 1/6/2020, last extension of the cash credit limit was granted.
The respondent No. 2 stood as Guarantor for the debtor - Ashish Shukla.

His signature is present on every page of the extension letter dated 1/6/2020 besides the signature of the Proprietor of M/s. Adiya Enterprises, which is Ashish Shukla;
- on 14/8/2020, a fresh registered deed of mortgage was executed by complainant/respondent No. 2 in favour of the Bank by which the complainant mortgaged his house at Morena for cash credit limit of Ashish Shukla.
In the mortgage deed, the complainant had mentioned that he is giving his property as security against the cash credit limit of Ashish Shukla;
- on 14/8/2020, a guarantee agreement was also executed by the complainant of which clause No. 1 stipulated that the guarantor will pay the dues of the principal debtor unconditioinally.

- Ashish Shukla passed away on 5/3/2021;
- on 12/5/2021, the bank sent a notice to Aditya Enterprises to deposit the outstanding amount and also requested the borrower to pay the money by selling the stock;
- on 25/05/2021, a request was once again made by the Bank to Aditya Enterprises to clear the dues and close the account.
These notices have been annexed to the petition as Annexure P/8 from page Nos. 80 to 83;

- on 7/6/2021, the Bank again sent a legal notice through their lawyer to borrowers as well as complainant requested them to pay the amount since the account of Ashish Shukla has been classified as NPA.
This notice is annexed to the petition as Annexrue P/8 at page 84 of the petition;

- as the aforementioned notices went without any reply, on 3/7/2021, notice under Section 13 of the Securitization and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (hereinafter shall be referred to as "SARFAESI Act), was issued to M/s Aditya Enterprises.

Same is Annexure P/10 to the petition;
- as there was no response, on 26/11/2021, a second notice under Section 13 (2) of the SARFAESI Act was sent to the present complainant.
Same is Annexure P/11 at page 96 to the petition;
- immediately thereafter upon receiving the same, within six months, the complainant filed a complaint against the present petitioner and co-accused persons on 18/4/2022.
Same is Annexure P/2 to the petition.
Pursuant to which statement under Section 200 Cr.P.C. were recorded in the said complaint case.

During the pendency of the complaint case itself, on 5/5/2022, a written complaint was submitted by respondent No. 2 to the police station Kotwali, District Morena without disclosing the fact that the private complaint based on the same facts was pending before the JMFC,
Morena in which the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was already dismissed.

Thereafter on 24/5/2022, the private complaint filed by the complainant was dismissed on merits by the Court below under Section 203 of Cr.P.C. and copy of the said order is at page 45 to the petition;
- on 3/6/2022, the impugned FIR was registered which is sought to be quashed by the petitioners.
The aforementioned are the undisputed sequence of the facts in this case.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has argued at length that the petitioners herein have only been made accused for discharging their official functions under the banking laws.

He further argued that after Ashish Shukla, the person who had taken the loan passed away, the Bank was at liberty under Section 13 (11) of the the SARFAESI Act to recover their dues as against the secured creditor from the guarantor.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that the respondent No.2 has the option under the law to prefer an appeal under the SARFAESI Act against the notice under Section 13 (2) issued to them by the bank.

Under the circumstances, it is urged on behalf of the petitioners that the FIR has maliciously been registered against the petitioners and that even if the entire allegations against the petitioners in the FIR are taken to be correct even then a prima facie case is not made out against the petitioners Nishkarsh Singhal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105638602/

Learned counsel for respondent No. 2 on the other hand submits that the petition ought to be dismissed as the case is still at the stage of investigation and the FIR discloses the commission of a cognizable offence.

In order to support his arguments, learned counsel for respondent No. 2 has argued that respondent No. 2 has intimated the petitioners herein that they should recover their dues by selling stock held by the deceased creditor purchased on the basis of the loan granted to him by the Bank.
He further states that had the Bank acted thus, it would have recovered its entire loss and there would be no necessity to issue notice to respondent No. 2 and harass him.

He has further submitted that the petitioners in collusion with the family members of the deceased creditor removed the stock and thereby have jeopardised the interest of respondent No. 2 who now faces the action by the bank.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the petition and documents filed therein.
As already stated that the fact recorded hereinabove are undisputed.

It is also undisputed that the petitioners herein are acting in the interest of the bank by attempting to recover the dues of the creditor from the respondent No. 2, who is the guarantor and in that capacity liable under Section 13 (11) of the the SARFAESI Act.

Learned counsel for respondent No. 2 was asked by this Court as to what are the facts/ prima facie evidence that he has to support his view that the petitioners in collusion with the family members of the deceased creditor had removed the stock held by the deceased creditor in order to escape their liability and shift the same to respondent No. 2.
Learned counsel for respondent no. 2 has submitted that the same is for the Police to investigate and unearth.
With great deference to learned counsel for respondent No. 2, the said contention cannot be acceded to.

If the Police is to act on a mere statement / allegation unsubstantiated by any kind of material evidence which would prima facie raised the doubt of an offence having been committed, then the same cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

Commercial and transactional offences always leave a paper trail and therefore, when an allegation is with regard to a white collar offence invariably their exists some documentary evidence or the other, to raise a prima facie suspicion of the police or the Court that perhaps what the complainant alleges is true.

In this case, it is clear that the respondent No. 2 has swung into action only to avoid his liability under the the SARFAESI Act as a guarantor and upon receiving a notice under Section 13(2) of the SARFAESI Act has filed the FIR against the petitioners.

It is also relevant to mention here that the complainant / respondent No. 2 has not disclosed this fact to the police that before registration of FIR that an application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. which was filed alongwith complaint under Section 200 by respondent No. 2, was dismissed by the learned JMFC.
This fact ought to have been mentioned in the FIR in order to disclose to the Police that before approaching to the Police, the respondent No. 2 had already exhausted his option before the JMFC.

sentences.text: It is also relevant to mention here that complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. was also subsequently dismissed by the learned Court below exercising jurisdiction under Section 203 of Cr.P.C.
Learned counsel for respondent No. 2 has mentioned that there is a criminal revision that has been filed by respondent No. 2 which is still pending before the Court of Sessions.
Learned counsel for the petitioners on the other hand submits that same has been filed as a response to the 482 petition filed by the petitioners herein in order to thwart any progress in this Case.

Looking at the facts and circumstances of the case, it is clear that the petitioners herein have only acted in the best interest of the institution and have attempted to recover the dues from the deceased/creditor through the respondent No. 2-guarantor.

The same is prima facie permissible under Section 13 (11) of the SARFAESI Act and therefore, issuing notices and attempting to recover the said dues from the respondent no. 2 cannot by any any stretch of imagination be levelled as a criminal offence much less under the Sections that have been registered by the Police.

Under the circumstances, the petition succeeds and further proceedings in Crime No. 561/2022 registered at Police Staton Kotwali, District Morena alongwith all the consequential proceedings, if any, stands quashed.
However, the right of respondent No. 2 to file an appeal under the SARFAESI Act is protected.
With the above, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
